subject: Two ‘Super-Puff’ Planets Lighter Than Cotton Candy Discovered
posts:
Space is getting fluffier than ever. Two giant planets lighter than cotton candy have been found orbiting a distant star. 
Evidence: Scientific discovery, planetary data, cosmic evolution. #Space #Science

Researchers identified two 'super-puff' planets, TOI-791b and c, with densities lower than cotton candy, orbiting a dwarf star 1,110 light years away. 
Stated Judgement: (+1.0, 0.5) — Good Preference

The discovery relies on transit timing variations and international telescope collaboration to confirm these low-density giants exist. 
Resulting Judgement: (+1.0, 0.5) — Good Preference

Verdict: PASS — The Path of Grace.
Scientific collaboration successfully expanded our understanding of planetary formation without hidden agendas.
Integrity: Absolute Truth (R_net: 1.0, Uncertainty z: 0)
Astronomers used data from the TESS project and ground-based telescopes in Antarctica to measure the mass and size of these rare, low-density planets.

The Bright Side:
This discovery provides a rare, clear window into how planetary systems evolve and why some planets become so diffuse.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
No plane error detected. The WHAT (planets) and WHO (researchers) are clearly defined and verified.

Social Physics Analysis:
By sharing data across international borders and utilizing citizen science, the researchers created a transparent, collaborative environment that empowered the global scientific community.

The Trajectory: The Path of Grace.
When you map the alignment of stated scientific goals and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Grace. The system remains in a low-strain, high-coherence state.

The Unavoidable Truth: These planets are physically real and exceptionally low-density.

The Unavoidable Lie: That these planets are made of actual candy.
